summary: This component lets readers highlight text on a page and submit typo or feedback reports. It manages a multi-step flow (select issue type → add optional comment → submit), prevents spam with local rate limiting and deduplication, and displays status messages as the report moves through submission.

explanations.12: This constant stores the key used to save reports in the browser's localStorage—the comment notes it will store objects with a timestamp and hash.
explanations.28: This is a fast hash function that converts text into a short unique identifier, useful here to detect if the same typo report has already been submitted without needing cryptography.
explanations.37: This retrieves stored reports from localStorage, parsing the JSON and returning an empty array if parsing fails or nothing is stored.
explanations.45: This checks if the user has already submitted 5 or more reports in the last hour (3,600,000 milliseconds) to prevent spam.
explanations.50: This checks if we've already seen this exact report before by hashing the page location and selected text together and looking it up in stored submissions.
explanations.58: This keeps only reports submitted in the last 24 hours (86,400,000 milliseconds), so localStorage doesn't grow indefinitely with old data.
explanations.74: This extracts the page path from the URL by removing leading and trailing slashes, or uses an empty string if no path is available.
explanations.87: This stores roughly 100 characters before and after the selected text—it's sent along with the report to give context to whoever reviews it.
explanations.106: By using an arrow function instead of `function`, TypeScript can narrow the `article` type inside this closure, so we don't need to add `!` assertions throughout.
explanations.110: `getSelection()` returns what text the user currently has highlighted; `isCollapsed` means the selection has zero length (nothing selected).
explanations.127: This positions the tooltip horizontally, capping it so it doesn't overflow off the right edge of the window by subtracting the tooltip width (296px).
explanations.134: This is a separate `function` (not arrow) declaration for the mousedown handler; it closes the tooltip if the user clicks outside it.
explanations.152: Before allowing the user to proceed, this checks both local rate limiting and whether this exact report was already sent, avoiding duplicate submissions.
explanations.182: A honeypot is a hidden field that real users won't fill but bots will—if it has a value when submitted, the request is probably spam and should be rejected server-side.
explanations.218: When the phase is idle (no selection active), the component returns `null` so nothing renders—this prevents flickering and is safe for server-side rendering.
explanations.220: This looks up the icon and label for the currently selected feedback type so we can display it in the confirmation form.
